annotations: Each row's category and public_note were proposed by this repository on 2026-09-27; the owner approved them the same day for a route's summary only ("In many cases there's an acceptable trail. Only provide the warnings if the route goes over the road."), so every row is display "route_only". US 340 is "speed", the category the owner added ("Yes, add 'speed' (Recommended)"). The westbound rows of 2026-09-28 (intersection, "Ramp traffic to and from DC 295 merges in and crosses the lanes.") were approved by the owner the same day: "Approve as written".

value.public_note: Freeway-grade highway with fast through traffic.

rows.reason: Legal but avoid. The owner, 2026-09-27, asked about US 340 in West Virginia (the William L. Wilson Freeway), chose "Legal but avoid" ("Leave access as OSM has it; the stress penalty (LTS 4) already pushes Default and calmer rides off it when there's an alternative.") and then: "Maybe make a 5th category for legal but to be avoided". The first entry of the category.
rows.evidence: OSM, Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: way 15561007, William L. Wilson Freeway, highway=trunk, ref US 340, maxspeed 45 mph, no bicycle tag, so bicycle-legal by default and LTS 4 by the classifier. Only this 1.05 km of the freeway is in the extract, which is built from the DC, Maryland and Virginia state files; the rest lies in West Virginia.

value.public_note: Bridge roadway shared with fast traffic; the Anacostia Riverwalk Trail beside it is the calmer crossing.

rows.reason: LTS 4. The owner, 2026-09-27: "11th street is LTS4, benning road by bridge on road, and south Capitol by bridge on a road are in the avoid category". This is the 11th Street Bridge local span or one of its south landing ways. They carried the crossings fixture's ordinary-ride penalty for the owner's "Steer to the path" (2026-09-26: "Keep it legal but add a penalty on that roadway for ordinary rides so the Riverwalk wins when it's close in length."); the owner retired that penalty on 2026-09-27 ("Retire it (Recommended)"), and this row's LTS 4 stress penalty now does the steering.
